metadata.case_name: CHIU YUEN YUEN v. BUCKINGHAM BANQUET LTD T/A BUCKINGHAM RESTAURANT

plaintiff.occupation_before: Housewife; worked part-time for her husband as a cashier assisting in his taxi rental business

source: When she arrived at Princess Margaret Hospital on 8 January 2015, there was swelling over her right ankle, and X-ray showed that her right ankle was fractured.
Both doctors concluded that the injuries to Madam Chiu’s right ankle were the direct result of the accident.
X-ray taken at the examination in February 2017 showed that the fracture had healed with good alignment with no arthritic changes and no other body abnormality.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the ankle or foot

manifestations.description: Swelling over her right ankle on arrival at hospital
Pain in right ankle after walking and standing for 30 minutes or more; intermittent pain on exertion
Some loss of flexibility of her right ankle in relation to its range of movement
Needed a stick to assist her for long journeys
Unable to swim (stopped an activity she enjoyed)
Required assistance for heavy household chores during prolonged treatment (10 months)

treatments_received.treatment: Admission to Princess Margaret Hospital and application of cast to right ankle; discharged with two crutches
source: When she arrived at Princess Margaret Hospital on 8 January 2015, there was swelling over her right ankle, and X-ray showed that her right ankle was fractured. She was hospitalised until 12 January 2015, during which a cast on her ankle was applied and she was discharged with two crutches to assist her to walk.
Her cast was removed on 10 March 2015, following which she had to receive physiotherapy from 8 April to 15 September 2015, a span of 5 months.

treatments_received.treatment: Physiotherapy from 8 April to 15 September 2015 (5 months)
source: Her cast was removed on 10 March 2015, following which she had to receive physiotherapy from 8 April to 15 September 2015, a span of 5 months.

treatments_received.treatment: Physiotherapy treatment for lower back pain from 29 September 2015 to 23 October 2015
source: On 29 September 2015, she complained of lower back pain and was examined again at the Department of Physiotherapy of Princess Margaret Hospital. She received treatment for this complaint and reported subjective improvement of 80% and treatment was stopped after the last session on 23 October 2015.

treatments_received.treatment: Analgesic medication (about twice a week) and topical ointment as required in bad weather
source: After these treatments, Madam Chiu complained that she would feel pain in her right ankle after walking and standing for 30 minutes or more, although the pain was relieved by about 50% by taking analgesic twice a week.
On raining or bad weather days, she would feel pain in her ankle, obliging her to take medication or apply ointment to alleviate her pain.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Unable to do household work during the period of prolonged treatment (10 months); deprivation of household services to family for that period.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Could no longer swim, which she enjoyed doing with her grandchildren.
Intermittent pain on exertion, reduced range of movement of right ankle, needed a stick for long journeys.

comparable_cases.injury_description: Fracture of right lower fibula; ankle injured; cast applied; some residual pain and stiffness of the ankle
